newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Advance of U.N. forensic team goes to Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Advance of U.N. forensic team goes to Zaire.

text.p: An advance party of four or five technical experts is expected to arrive in Goma, eastern Zaire on Monday to begin probing alleged massacres of Rwandan Hutus and civilians, a U.N. spokesman said on Friday.

The United Nations announced in Geneva earlier this week that the team, which includes forensic experts, was not scheduled to arrive in the region until May 4 but U.N. spokesman Fred Eckhard said several technical and security personnel would go earlier.
Zairean rebels, who have captured half of Zaire since taking up arms last October, have given the green light for the mission to the eastern border town of Goma.

The inquiry was demanded by the U.N. human rights investigator for Zaire, Roberto Garreton, who accused the rebels of massacring thousands of Rwandan Hutu refugees and civilians after he visited Goma earlier this month and spoke to witnesses.
The rebels shelled and overran the camps late last year, after which more than half a million Rwandan Hutus returned home while up to 250,000 others fled deeper into Zaire.
The Hutus fled to Zaire after Tutsi rebels ended the Hutu-led genocide of minority Tutsis in Rwanda in 1994, during which many among the refugees killed or watched others kill.

The U.N. commission of inquiry will include Garreton and two other U.N. investigators and three U.N. human rights officials from Geneva. They will be joined by three forensic scientists who will stay in Goma for a month.

Garreton's attempts to visit several massacre sites in Goma had been thwarted by the rebels, and it remains to be seen whether they will allow Western forensic experts to dig up mass graves in the area for a whole month.
